You are a read-only survey worker for prover lane `ajc-p3`. Project: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (Lean 4 + mathlib). Do NOT edit any file. Report facts with file:line citations.

TASK. I need an honest, skeptical inventory of the body-position `sorry`s that sit between this project and PICARD / Pic^0 REPRESENTABILITY, so I can rank them by value. For EACH file below, list every `sorry` with its line number, the FULL statement of the enclosing declaration (verbatim binders + conclusion), and then answer: (a) what does discharging it buy downstream — who consumes it (grep for the declaration name); (b) is the statement non-vacuous, i.e. does it actually mention the curve / the Picard object it claims to be about, and are its hypotheses inhabitable (is there an instance or witness for each class/hypothesis it binds?); (c) how hard does it look, and does its stated prerequisite ALREADY EXIST in the file or project (check with `/home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon search "<words>" --json`, which spans both workspace projects and mathlib)?

Files, in priority order:
1. `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0Et.lean` (2 sorries)
2. `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` (2 sorries)
3. `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (3 sorries)
4. `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean` (2) and `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/QuotRepresentability.lean` (1)
5. `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SerreFiniteness.lean` (2)
6. `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean` (1)

Then, separately, report on the roadmap item `AJC.picrep.tensor` ("Pullback-tensor and fibre base change"): find the Lean declaration(s) it corresponds to. The blueprint frontier lists a `[sorry]` node "The canonical pullback--tensor comparison is an isomorphism (lemma)" with 58 unlocks / 2 uses. Find that Lean declaration by name, quote its statement, list its 2 use sites, and say what is actually missing in its proof.

IMPORTANT — the bar. A 2026-07-29 audit of this workspace refuted 99 of 101 sampled representability claims: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS (the statement did not mention the object it claimed to be about), 12 proved something adjacent. So for each item, explicitly say whether the STATEMENT is worth proving, not just whether it is provable. Flag any declaration whose hypotheses are uninhabitable (a class with no instance) or whose statement omits the curve.

Be terse per item but complete on the list. Cite file:line for everything.
